This is the R twin of the Python guide
[`distributions-for-actuaries-counts-aggregates.md`](distributions-for-actuaries-counts-aggregates.md).
It recomputes the worked examples and problem answers of chapters 3 and 4 and
the aggregate limits of section 6.4 of CAS Monograph 2, *Distributions for
Actuaries* by David Bahnemann (2015). The sections, examples and numbers are the
same, because the R package runs the same Rust code. Read the Python guide for
the discussion of each result. The companion R guide,
[`distributions-for-actuaries-claim-size.qmd`](distributions-for-actuaries-claim-size.qmd),
covers chapters 2, 5 and 6. `R/prospicio/tests/test-guides.R` requires each
chunk to print exactly the text under it.

## 1. Translating the parameters

| Monograph | prospicio (R) |
|---|---|
| Poisson λ | `poisson_count(λ)` |
| binomial (m, p) | `binomial_count(m, p)` |
| negative binomial (α, ν), Var = ν + ν²/α | `negative_binomial_count(α, ν/α)` |
| mean ν and contagion γ | `claim_count(ν, 1 + γν)` |
| Poisson mixed by a gamma with mean ν and shape α | `mixed_poisson_count(ν, 1/√α, "gamma")` |
| method of moments | `negative_binomial_count_from_mean_variance(m, v)` |
| any count on 0, 1, 2, ... | `empirical_count(probs)` |

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(prospicio)

num <- function(x, digits = 0) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
show <- function(label, book, ours, digits = 4) {
  cat(sprintf("%-40s book %12s   prospicio %12s\n", label, num(book, digits), num(ours, digits)))
}
vec <- function(x, digits = 4) {
  paste0("[", paste(formatC(round(x, digits), format = "f", digits = digits), collapse = ", "), "]")
}
chi_square <- function(observed, probs) {
  e <- sum(observed) * probs
  sum((observed - e)^2 / e)
}
```

## 2. The Poisson and the binomial

```{r}
#| label: poisson
show("Ex 3.1  30 days, Pr{N = 0}", 0.9138, pmf(binomial_count(30, 0.003), 0))
show("        30 days, Pr{N = 1}", 0.0825, pmf(binomial_count(30, 0.003), 1))
show("        365 days, Pr{N = 2}", 0.2009, pmf(binomial_count(365, 0.003), 2))
for (case in list(list(1.0, c(0.9608, 0.0384, 0.0008)), list(1.5, c(0.9418, 0.0565, 0.0017)))) {
  for (n in 0:2) {
    show(sprintf("Ex 3.2  %.1f years, Pr{N = %d}", case[[1]], n), case[[2]][n + 1],
         pmf(poisson_count(0.04 * case[[1]]), n))
  }
}
cat("P3.4   Pr{N = 2}   book ", vec(c(0.0012, 0.0069, 0.0164)), "\n")
cat("                   ours ", vec(sapply(c(6, 15, 24), function(m) pmf(poisson_count(0.10 * m / 12), 2))), "\n")

policies <- c(868, 118, 11, 2, 1)
lam <- sum((0:4) * policies) / sum(policies)
p <- poisson_count(lam)
show("Ex 3.3  rate", 0.15, lam, 2)
cat("        pmf   book ", vec(c(0.8607, 0.1291, 0.0097, 0.0005)), "\n")
cat("              ours ", vec(pmf(p, 0:3)), "\n")
show("        chi-square", 2.43, chi_square(c(868, 118, 14), c(pmf(p, 0), pmf(p, 1), 1 - cdf(p, 1))), 2)
show("Ex 3.8  Pr{N >= 5}, 100 x 0.035", 0.2746, 1 - cdf(poisson_count(3.5), 4))
for (case in list(c(2.5, 0.7576), c(6.25, 0.1303), c(2.0, 0.8571), c(4.0, 0.4335))) {
  show(sprintf("P3.3   Pr{N <= 3}, rate %s", format(case[1])), case[2], cdf(poisson_count(case[1]), 3))
}
show("P3.30  Pr{N >= 6}, 20 cars x 0.30", 0.5543, 1 - cdf(poisson_count(6), 5))
show("P3.31  policies with a claim, of 8,000", 624, 8000 * (1 - pmf(poisson_count(650 / 8000), 0)), 0)
```

## 3. Parameter uncertainty: mixed Poissons

```{r}
#| label: mixed
rates <- c(0.10, 0.35, 0.70, 1.40); weights <- c(0.20, 0.40, 0.30, 0.10)
mixed <- sapply(0:5, function(n) sum(weights * sapply(rates, function(r) pmf(poisson_count(r), n))))
m <- sum(weights * rates)
v <- m + sum(weights * rates^2) - m^2
cat("Ex 3.4  mixed pmf     book ", vec(c(0.6365, 0.2556, 0.0788, 0.0218, 0.0056, 0.0013)), "\n")
cat("                      ours ", vec(mixed), "\n")
cat("        Poisson 0.51  book ", vec(c(0.6005, 0.3063, 0.0781, 0.0133, 0.0017, 0.0002)), "\n")
cat("                      ours ", vec(pmf(poisson_count(m), 0:5)), "\n")
show("        Var[N]", 0.6439, v)
geo <- mixed_poisson_count(0.25, 1, "gamma")
cat("Ex 3.5  pmf           book ", vec(c(0.8, 0.16, 0.032, 0.0064, 0.0013, 0.0003)), "\n")
cat("                      ours ", vec(pmf(geo, 0:5)), "\n")
cat("        geometric          ", vec(pmf(geometric_count(0.25), 0:5)), "\n")
show("        Var[N]", 0.3125, variance(geo))

nb <- negative_binomial_count(2, 1)
show("P3.11  mean", 2, mean(nb), 0)
show("       variance", 4, variance(nb), 0)
show("       Pr{N <= 3}", 0.8125, cdf(nb, 3))
nb <- negative_binomial_count_from_mean_variance(0.100, 0.100 + 0.005)
cat("P3.12  pmf   book ", vec(c(0.9070, 0.0864, 0.0062, 0.0004)), "\n")
cat("             ours ", vec(pmf(nb, 0:3)), "\n")
show("P3.13  Var, Poisson 0.75", 0.7500, variance(poisson_count(0.75)))
show("       Var, two-point mixture", 0.8175, 0.75 + (0.75 * 0.6^2 + 0.25 * 1.2^2 - 0.75^2))
show("       Var, exponential mixture", 1.3125, variance(mixed_poisson_count(0.75, 1)))
```

## 4. The negative binomial and contagion

```{r}
#| label: negbin
nb_moments <- function(counts) {
  k <- seq_along(counts) - 1
  m1 <- sum(k * counts) / sum(counts)
  c(m1, sum(k^2 * counts) / sum(counts) - m1^2)
}
for (case in list(list("Ex 3.6", c(4429, 528, 39, 3, 1), c(0.1238, 2.44285, 0.7753)),
                  list("P3.15", c(8956, 907, 120, 15, 2), c(0.1200, 0.685714, 0.3288)))) {
  mv <- nb_moments(case[[2]])
  nb <- negative_binomial_count_from_mean_variance(mv[1], mv[2])
  probs <- c(pmf(nb, 0:2), 1 - cdf(nb, 2))
  observed <- c(case[[2]][1:3], sum(case[[2]][-(1:3)]))
  show(paste(case[[1]], "mean"), case[[3]][1], mv[1])
  show(paste(case[[1]], "alpha = r"), case[[3]][2], nb@r, 5)
  show(paste(case[[1]], "chi-square"), case[[3]][3], chi_square(observed, probs))
}
mv <- nb_moments(c(4429, 528, 39, 3, 1))
cat("Ex 3.6 pmf   book ", vec(c(0.8862, 0.1044, 0.0087, 0.0006)), "\n")
cat("             ours ", vec(pmf(negative_binomial_count_from_mean_variance(mv[1], mv[2]), 0:3)), "\n")

nb <- claim_count(1, 1 + 0.2 * 1)
cat("P3.28  pmf   book ", vec(c(0.4019, 0.3349, 0.1674, 0.0651, 0.0217, 0.0065)), "\n")
cat("             ours ", vec(pmf(nb, 0:5)), "\n")
contagion <- function(counts) {
  m <- sum(sapply(counts, mean)); v <- sum(sapply(counts, variance))
  (v - m) / m^2
}
show("Ex 3.9  20 policies, nu 0.15, gamma 0.4", 0.020,
     contagion(rep(list(claim_count(0.15, 1 + 0.4 * 0.15)), 20)), 3)
show("P3.29  three lines", 0.1000,
     contagion(list(claim_count(10, 1 + 0.35 * 10), claim_count(25, 1 + 0.20 * 25), poisson_count(5))))
```

## 5. Aggregate claims and their moments

`compound_distribution()` uses Panjer's recursion by default. Pass
`method = "fft"` for the FFT, as the Python guide does. R indexes from 1, so the
probability of a total of `k` steps is `probs[k + 1]`.

```{r}
#| label: aggregate
agg <- compound_distribution(empirical_count(c(0.6, 0.3, 0.1)),
                             grid_distribution(100, c(0, 0.4, 0.5, 0.1)), 16, method = "fft")
cat("Ex 4.1  F_S   book ", vec(c(0.6, 0.72, 0.886, 0.956, 0.989, 0.999, 1.0)), "\n")
cat("              ours ", vec(cdf(agg, 100 * (0:6))), "\n")
show("        E[S]", 85, mean(agg), 0)
show("        Var[S]", 15055, variance(agg), 0)
agg <- compound_distribution(empirical_count(c(0.20, 0.40, 0.25, 0.15)),
                             grid_distribution(500, c(0, 0.1, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2)), 16, method = "fft")
cat("P4.1   F_S   book ", vec(c(0.2, 0.24, 0.4025, 0.5427, 0.6795, 0.758, 0.8418, 0.9047, 0.9507)), "\n")
cat("             ours ", vec(cdf(agg, 500 * (0:8))), "\n")

m <- compound_moments(poisson_count(2.5), gamma_distribution(3, 400))
show("Ex 4.2  E[S]", 3000, m[["mean"]], 0)
show("        Var[S]", 4800000, m[["variance"]], 0)
show("        skewness", 0.9129, m[["skew"]])
poisson_gamma_cdf <- function(s, lam, shape, scale, terms = 400) {
  n <- poisson_count(lam)
  if (s <= 0) return(pmf(n, 0))
  k <- 1:(terms - 1)
  pmf(n, 0) + sum(pmf(n, k) * sapply(k, function(j) cdf(gamma_distribution(shape * j, scale), s)))
}
S <- c(0, 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 6000, 8000, 10000)
cat("        F(s)  book ", vec(c(0.0821, 0.1096, 0.1867, 0.3755, 0.5613, 0.7152, 0.9013, 0.9723, 0.9934)), "\n")
cat("              ours ", vec(sapply(S, poisson_gamma_cdf, lam = 2.5, shape = 3, scale = 400)), "\n")
```

## 6. Approximations by matching moments

```{r}
#| label: approximations
cases <- list(
  list("Table 4.3", 4, 2.5, 3, 400, c(0, 2000, 4000, 6000, 8000),
       c(0.0821, 0.3755, 0.7152, 0.9013, 0.9723), c(0.0855, 0.3240, 0.6760, 0.9145, 0.9888),
       c(0.0459, 0.3680, 0.7185, 0.9038, 0.9724)),
  list("Table 4.4", 5, 10, 0.05, 6000, c(0, 2000, 6000, 10000, 18000),
       c(0.00005, 0.5922, 0.8401, 0.9294, 0.9846), c(0.2451, 0.4090, 0.7549, 0.9463, 0.9997),
       c(0.1228, 0.5886, 0.8402, 0.9298, 0.9847)),
  list("P4.13", 4, 8, 0.2, 3750, c(0, 3000, 9000, 15000, 27000),
       c(0.0003, 0.3420, 0.7774, 0.9349, 0.9954), c(0.1241, 0.2819, 0.7181, 0.9584, 1.0000),
       c(0.0263, 0.3362, 0.7782, 0.9356, 0.9953))
)
for (cs in cases) {
  freq <- poisson_count(cs[[3]]); sev <- gamma_distribution(cs[[4]], cs[[5]]); S <- cs[[6]]
  m <- compound_moments(freq, sev)
  approx <- function(kind) sapply(S, function(s) approximation_cdf(moment_approximation(freq, sev, kind), s))
  exact <- sapply(S, poisson_gamma_cdf, lam = cs[[3]], shape = cs[[4]], scale = cs[[5]])
  cat(sprintf("%s: mean %s, sd %s, skewness %.4f\n", cs[[1]], num(m[["mean"]]),
              num(sqrt(m[["variance"]])), m[["skew"]]))
  first <- function(x) {
    paste0("[", paste(c(formatC(round(x[1], cs[[2]]), format = "f", digits = cs[[2]]),
                        formatC(round(x[-1], 4), format = "f", digits = 4)), collapse = ", "), "]")
  }
  cat("  exact          book ", first(cs[[7]]), "\n")
  cat("                 ours ", first(exact), "\n")
  cat("  normal         book ", vec(cs[[8]]), "\n")
  cat("                 ours ", vec(approx("normal")), "\n")
  cat("  shifted gamma  book ", vec(cs[[9]]), "\n")
  cat("                 ours ", vec(approx("shifted_gamma")), "\n")
  cat("  shifted lognormal   ", vec(approx("shifted_lognormal")), "\n")
}
```

## 7. Recursion and Fourier inversion

```{r}
#| label: recursion
agg <- compound_distribution(poisson_count(1.75), grid_distribution(1000, c(0, 0.20, 0.40, 0.20, 0.15, 0.05)), 64)
cat("Ex 4.4  f_S   book ", vec(c(0.1738, 0.0608, 0.1323, 0.1046, 0.117, 0.0932, 0.0786, 0.0641)), "\n")
cat("              ours ", vec(agg@probs[1:8]), "\n")
cat("        F_S at 9,000, 12,000, 16,000  book ", vec(c(0.9121, 0.9729, 0.9955)), "\n")
cat("                                      ours ", vec(cdf(agg, c(9000, 12000, 16000))), "\n")

S <- c(500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 6000, 10000)
for (case in list(list(100, c(0.1158, 0.1956, 0.3852, 0.7218, 0.9042, 0.9937)),
                  list(20, c(0.1108, 0.1885, 0.3775, 0.7165, 0.9019, 0.9935)))) {
  h <- case[[1]]
  grid <- discretize(gamma_distribution(3, 400), h, 6000 / h + 1, "rounding")
  agg <- compound_distribution(poisson_count(2.5), grid, 30000 / h)
  cat(sprintf("Ex 4.5  step %3.0f  grid mean %s  variance %s\n", h, num(mean(grid), 2), num(variance(grid))))
  cat("        F_S  book ", vec(case[[2]]), "\n")
  cat("             ours ", vec(cdf(agg, S)), "\n")
}
agg <- compound_distribution(poisson_count(1.35), grid_distribution(500, c(0, 0.1, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2)), 64)
cat("P4.16   F_S  book ", vec(c(0.2592, 0.2942, 0.4366, 0.5606, 0.6838, 0.8306, 0.9223, 0.967, 0.9872)), "\n")
cat("             ours ", vec(cdf(agg, c(0, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 6000))), "\n")

grid <- discretize(gamma_distribution(3, 400), 1, 20001, "local_moment")
agg <- compound_distribution(poisson_count(2.5), grid, 2^16, method = "fft")
S <- c(500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 6000, 8000, 10000)
cat("Ex 4.7  Heckman-Meyers  book ", vec(c(0.1094, 0.1869, 0.3757, 0.5614, 0.7151, 0.9011, 0.9722, 0.9934)), "\n")
cat("        exact series         ", vec(sapply(S, poisson_gamma_cdf, lam = 2.5, shape = 3, scale = 400)), "\n")
cat("        FFT                  ", vec(cdf(agg, S)), "\n")
cat(sprintf("        aliasing error below 1e-12: %s\n", agg@report$aliasing_error < 1e-12))

size <- gamma_distribution(2.5, 500)
show("Ex 4.8  E[X; 2,000]", 1147, lev(size, 2000), 0)
show("        mass at the limit", 0.1562, survival(size, 2000))
show("        jump in F_S at 2,000", 0.0552, pmf(poisson_count(1.308), 1) * survival(size, 2000))
```

## 8. Simulation

```{r}
#| label: simulation
years <- total(total(simulate_events(poisson_count(2.5), gamma_distribution(3, 400), 10000, 2015)))
sim <- cdf(years, 3000)
exact <- poisson_gamma_cdf(3000, 2.5, 3, 400)
cat(sprintf("Ex 4.14  F(3,000): book's sample 0.5599, exact %.4f, within two standard errors here: %s\n",
            exact, abs(sim - exact) < 2 * sqrt(exact * (1 - exact) / 10000)))
cat(sprintf("Ex 4.13  lognormal (4.956; 2.3), 1.5 claims a year: E[S] = %s (book 3,000)\n",
            num(1.5 * mean(lognormal(4.956, 2.3)))))
```

## 9. Aggregate limits

Ex 6.6's lognormal has μ = 7.6, not the printed 7.000 (see the Python guide).
The stop-loss of the shifted gamma is a gamma's. It uses the `parameters` (shape,
scale and shift) of `moment_approximation()`.

```{r}
#| label: aggregate-limits
size <- lognormal(7.6, 2.4)
count <- claim_count(1.2, 1 + 0.1 * 1.2)
basic <- mean(count) * lev(size, 500e3)
show("Ex 6.6  E[S], 500K per claim", 26092, basic, 0)
show("        E[S], 2M per claim", 34006, mean(count) * lev(size, 2e6), 0)
h <- 250
capped_2m <- discretize(size, h, 2e6 / h + 1, "local_moment")
m <- compound_moments(count, capped_2m)
show("        sd of S, 2M per claim", 151311, sqrt(m[["variance"]]), 0)
show("        skewness", 9.4728, m[["skew"]])

shifted_gamma_excess <- function(severity, L) {
  a <- moment_approximation(count, severity, "shifted_gamma")$parameters
  stop_loss(gamma_distribution(a[["shape"]], a[["scale"]]), L - a[["shift"]])
}
sg <- shifted_gamma_excess(capped_2m, 3e6)
agg <- compound_distribution(count, capped_2m, 2^16, method = "fft")
exact <- stop_loss(agg, 3e6)
show("Ex 6.6  removed by a 3M aggregate limit", 91, sg, 0)
cat(sprintf("        the same by FFT, exactly: %s\n", num(exact)))
show("        I(2M, 3M), shifted gamma", 1.2998, (m[["mean"]] - sg) / basic)
cat(sprintf("        I(2M, 3M), exact: %.4f\n", (m[["mean"]] - exact) / basic))
```


```{r}
#| label: table-6-4
book <- list(
  list(1e6, c(1e6, 2e6, 3e6, 5e6), c(29702, 30306, 30333, 30335)),
  list(2e6, c(2e6, 3e6, 5e6), c(33524, 33915, 34002)),
  list(3e6, c(3e6, 5e6), c(35421, 35781)),
  list(5e6, 5e6, 37428)
)
cat(sprintf("%9s %9s %8s %9s %8s\n", "per claim", "aggregate", "book", "sh. gamma", "exact"))
exact_at <- list()
for (row in book) {
  l <- row[[1]]
  grid <- discretize(size, h, l / h + 1, "local_moment")
  moments <- compound_moments(count, grid)
  agg <- compound_distribution(count, grid, 2^16, method = "fft")
  for (j in seq_along(row[[2]])) {
    L <- row[[2]][j]
    sg <- moments[["mean"]] - shifted_gamma_excess(grid, L)
    cat(sprintf("%8.0fM %8.0fM %8s %9s %8s\n", l / 1e6, L / 1e6, num(row[[3]][j]), num(sg), num(lev(agg, L))))
  }
  exact_at[[as.character(l)]] <- c(at_l = lev(agg, l), unlimited = mean(agg))
}
for (case in list(c(1e6, 0.0209), c(2e6, 0.0142), c(3e6, 0.0112), c(5e6, 0.0081))) {
  e <- exact_at[[as.character(case[1])]]
  cat(sprintf("P6.11  aggregate limit = per-claim limit %.0fM: share removed, book %.4f, exact %.4f\n",
              case[1] / 1e6, case[2], 1 - e[["at_l"]] / e[["unlimited"]]))
}
e <- exact_at[["1e+06"]]
show("P6.12  premium, 1M per claim, v = 25%", 40447, e[["unlimited"]] / 0.75, 0)
cat(sprintf("P6.12  credit for a 1M aggregate limit: book 844, exact %s\n",
            num((e[["unlimited"]] - e[["at_l"]]) / 0.75)))
```
